issue.description: MultiTLDHandler and BulkHandler in internal/server/handlers_api.go both wait for every parallel RDAP check in the batch to finish before writing any response bytes (writeJSONResponse is called once, after bulkResult is fully assembled). For a 5-TLD multi-check this means the caller sees nothing until the slowest registry in the batch responds, even though faster registries (Verisign at 10 req/s) finish well before slower ones (Google at 1 req/s). Add a streaming response mode -- Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream) or newline-delimited JSON -- that emits each per-domain result as it completes rather than buffering the whole batch. Ties into the plan's own 'Instant feel' web UI design goal (~100-200ms results) which currently only holds for single-domain checks, not multi-TLD/bulk. Keep the existing single-JSON-response mode as the default for backward compatibility; add streaming as an opt-in via an Accept header or query parameter.

issue.description: The CLI check subcommand (internal/cli/check.go) already has clean scriptable exit codes (0=available, 1=taken, 2=error) which is great for CI gating, but there's no way to sit and wait for a domain to drop without the caller writing their own polling loop. Add a --watch flag to the check subcommand: re-run the check on an interval (default e.g. 5m, configurable), print each result, and exit 0 the moment the domain becomes available (or run indefinitely with --watch --forever). This is the zero-infrastructure precursor to the server-side webhook watch feature in ADR-001 (docs/plan/plan.md) -- ships independently, needs no new storage or server changes, and is immediately useful to the exact audience (self-hosters, CI/scripting users) who already prefer the CLI. Respect the existing per-registry rate limiter so a long-running watch loop doesn't hammer the registry.
issue.title: CLI: add --watch flag for polling a domain until it becomes available
